reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 (Intrinsic Function amendment) both arguments of FUNCTION REM must be class numeric (an arithmetic expression: numeric item, numeric literal, numeric/integer function, expression); an alphanumeric, alphabetic, numeric-edited or group item, a nonnumeric literal, a nonnumeric figurative or ALL literal, or an alphanumeric function must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: IntroducedIn/RemovedIn window; REM is IntroducedIn 85, so it binds at 85
per-position predicates asked only where p.AppliesAt(year); REM's Uniform('n') row has no predicates, so the class test is identical at every edition

reader.notes: Numeric-edited items are correctly classed alphanumeric. The refusal message says 'alphanumeric or national' for a figurative and cites §2023:15.77.3 at --std 85, cosmetic only.

refuter.evidence: Argument class numeric means 'An arithmetic expression must be specified' (§1989:A.2.2), and the 1985 arithmetic expression admits the figurative constant ZERO (§1985:VI.6.2.1), a form the reader did not probe.
